newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts to target 114-06 on upside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts to target 114-06 on upside.

text.p: September gilts will aim for 114-06 on Thursday, provided they can break above initial resistance at 113-23, technical analysts said.
"What we're seeing at the moment is a correction of the gains from around 111-30 to 114-18," said Lynn Branigan, technical analyst at MCM YieldWatch here.
"There's initial resistance at the intra-day high at 113-23, but if we turn back over there, it puts the corrective losses on hold, opening up the way for gains to 114-06."
By 0735 GMT, September gilts were up 5/32 at 113-20 after briefly touching 113-23 earlier in the session.
Branigan said 114-06 would likely cap any gains on Thursday, preventing a move in the immediate term to new contract highs above 114-31.
Carol Harmer, a trader and analyst at Kempton's Technical Analysis, agreed a recovery looked likely in Thursday's session given the oversold conditions of the short term charts.

"Good nearby resistance is at 113-25, 26 and this area is pivotal," she said from LIFFE. "I would buy a break above here as this would trigger further rallies with the 114-00 resistance looking to entice."
Harmer said as long as the contract held above 114-00 there would be pressure to the upside targeting 114-08.
On the downside, Branigan said there was support at 113-12, just ahead of 113-08, the 50 percent retracement of the rally from 111-30 to 114-18.
Below there, there was strong support at the June 10 low of 113-04 will kick in, a level which should hold the market near term.
"But if we do go through there, there's support at 112-30, the 62 percent retracement of that rally," said Branigan. "That would indicate that it's more than a correction, but a turn in sentiment."
By 0754 GMT, September short sterling was down one basis point at 93.05 and December was down 0.01 at 92.87.

Traders at a major British bank said Wednesday's sharp down moves were unlikely to be reversed as concerns about interest rates were being compounded by worries of higher consumer spending due to windfall payments.
"Sell into strength," said one trader. "I can see December down to 92.75." He put support for the September contract at 93.05, December at 92.85 and March at 92.75.
"When the market is as nervous as this it tends to hug the psychological numbers," he said.
